meta.title: Release Automation — KB Labs
meta.description: One plugin we ship 150+ packages through — every time, one command.

checks.title: Not just a list of commands.
checks.lead: Each check is an object with control over where and how it runs. Checks can be overridden at the flow level — platform and SDK have their own sets.

pipeline.title: Eight steps. Strict order.

stages.label: Lint
stages.detail: ESLint across all affected packages. Fast — only what changed.

stages.label: Type-check
stages.detail: tsc project references in dependency order. Catches cross-package type errors.

stages.label: Test
stages.detail: Vitest with coverage. Skips packages with no changed files.

stages.label: AI Review
stages.detail: LLM reviews the diff for logic errors, security issues, and style violations.

stages.label: QA Gate
stages.detail: Package-level quality checks. Fails if degradation is detected.

stages.label: Impact
stages.detail: Dependency graph analysis — which packages and tests are actually affected.

stages.label: Build
stages.detail: Topological build with DTS. Only changed packages + dependents rebuild.

stages.label: Release
stages.detail: Publish to npm + GitHub Release with changelog. Gated by all prior stages.

pipeline.subtitle: Each step can run standalone. Each fails explicitly — with a clear message.

config.title: Everything in one file. No extra config.
config.lead: Config lives in {configFile} alongside other KB Labs settings. No separate {releaseConfig}.
items: release.workflow — path to the release workflow YAML
release.targets — which packages to include in the pipeline
release.gates — required stages that must pass before publish
release.aiReview — model and prompt config for AI review step
release.npm — registry URL, access level, and publish token

items.title: Workflows as code, not config
items.detail: Release pipelines live in YAML under version control — reviewed, diffable, and revertable like any other change. No GUI state to export, no vendor format to migrate from.

items.title: Every stage is a plugin
items.detail: Lint, review, QA, deploy — each step is a typed plugin with declared capabilities. Swap any stage without touching the rest of the pipeline.

items.title: Fail fast, trace everything
items.detail: Stages run in order with explicit dependencies. The first failure stops the pipeline. Every run is fully traced: inputs, outputs, timing, and plugin calls.

hero.description: One plugin covers the full cycle: checks, build, changelog, npm publish, git tag. No scripts, no Notion runbook, no "I think I forgot to push the tag".

flows.title: Independent releases for different parts of the monorepo.
flows.configNote: A flow fully replaces the global {code} config — it doesn't merge. Packages are selected by glob patterns.

runs.note: Runs lint → type-check → test → AI review → build → publish. Only changed packages.
Force full pipeline regardless of git state. Used for major releases.

flows.lead2: Platform and SDK release independently — one command each. 150+ packages, but never everything at once.
flows.lead1: A flow is a named release profile. It fully replaces three things: which packages to build, the versioning strategy, and the set of checks. Everything else (registry, changelog, git) comes from the global config.

solutionReleaseAutomation.changelogNote: Four built-in templates: {templates}. If the LLM is unavailable — falls back to a plain commit list.
